safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention neck stiffness (present/absent).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In an acute severe headache, documenting absence of neck stiffness helps rule out meningitis/subarachnoid hemorrhage red-flag features and supports safe triage. If omitted, subsequent clinicians may treat this as “not assessed,” potentially prompting unnecessary escalation or delaying confident outpatient management.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not document presence/absence of fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is a key associated symptom for infectious causes of headache; documenting its absence supports lower-risk assessment. Omission can lead to uncertainty about red-flag screening and may alter follow-up/triage decisions even if the patient was afebrile.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether paracetamol relieved symptoms informs severity assessment and guides next-step analgesic selection/escalation for suspected migraine/tension headache.
